{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015BaqDzN1VAbvGChwyRaAkp","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t/**\n2\t * The part of a workshop recording a member can actually replay after its configured start offset.\n3\t *\n4\t * Note: The offset removes only the waiting-room part of a replay. It never changes the underlying YouTube video or\n5\t *       the live workshop schedule.\n6\t */\n7\texport function getWorkshopRecordingDurationSeconds(\n8\t    totalVideoDurationSeconds: number | null,\n9\t    recordingStartOffsetSeconds: number,\n10\t): number | null {\n11\t    if (\n12\t        totalVideoDurationSeconds === null ||\n13\t        !Number.isSafeInteger(totalVideoDurationSeconds) ||\n14\t        totalVideoDurationSeconds <= 0 ||\n15\t        !Number.isSafeInteger(recordingStartOffsetSeconds) ||\n16\t        recordingStartOffsetSeconds < 0\n17\t    ) {\n18\t        return null;\n19\t    }\n20\t\n21\t    const recordingDurationSeconds = totalVideoDurationSeconds - recordingStartOffsetSeconds;\n22\t    return recordingDurationSeconds > 0 ? recordingDurationSeconds : null;\n23\t}\n24\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c05e6a4c-57b2-46a2-a684-8190a40c180e","uuid":"63cce8c0-64a7-4288-94d0-7e806dc34fbf","timestamp":"2026-09-16T18:01:56.243Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\lib\\workshops\\workshopRecordingDuration.ts","content":"/**\n * The part of a workshop recording a member can actually replay after its configured start offset.\n *\n * Note: The offset removes only the waiting-room part of a replay. It never changes the underlying YouTube video or\n *       the live workshop schedule.\n */\nexport function getWorkshopRecordingDurationSeconds(\n    totalVideoDurationSeconds: number | null,\n    recordingStartOffsetSeconds: number,\n): number | null {\n    if (\n        totalVideoDurationSeconds === null ||\n        !Number.isSafeInteger(totalVideoDurationSeconds) ||\n        totalVideoDurationSeconds <= 0 ||\n        !Number.isSafeInteger(recordingStartOffsetSeconds) ||\n        recordingStartOffsetSeconds < 0\n    ) {\n        return null;\n    }\n\n    const recordingDurationSeconds = totalVideoDurationSeconds - recordingStartOffsetSeconds;\n    return recordingDurationSeconds > 0 ? recordingDurationSeconds : null;\n}\n","numLines":24,"startLine":1,"totalLines":24}}}

 const isSlugOffered = !roomCapabilities.isSlugFixed;\n55\t    const isReactionSettingOffered = isWorkshopPanelOfferedByKind(workshop.kind, 'reactions');\n56\t    const isWatchingCountSettingOffered = {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01PJEoZhduUdLeCYF8hQZWtW","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport { formatCzechCountedNoun } from '@/lib/language/czechNumbers';\n2\t\n3\tconst CZECH_DATE_TIME_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ', { dateStyle: 'short', timeStyle: 'short' });\n4\tconst CZECH_CLOCK_TIME_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ', { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });\n5\tconst CZECH_DAY_TIME_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ', {\n6\t    day: 'numeric',\n7\t    month: 'numeric',\n8\t    hour: '2-digit',\n9\t    minute: '2-digit',\n10\t});\n11\tconst CZECH_DAY_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ', { day: 'numeric', month: 'numeric' });\n12\t\n13\t/**\n14\t * A span of time which is still read as a clock, above which the day has to be named as well\n15\t */\n16\tconst WHOLE_DAY_MILLISECONDS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000;\n17\t\n18\t/**\n19\t * Formats a server timestamp consistently across the workshop administration.\n20\t */\n21\texport function formatWorkshopAdminDateTime(timestamp: string): string {\n22\t    return CZECH_DATE_TIME_FORMAT.format(new Date(timestamp));\n23\t}\n24\t\n25\t/**\n26\t * Names one moment of the overview graph as shortly as the shown span allows\n27\t *\n28\t * Note: An hour-long workshop is read as a clock, a week of a permanent room by the day, so the axis never repeats the\n29\t *       very same date under every single tick.\n30\t */\n31\texport function formatWorkshopOverviewAxisTime(timestampMilliseconds: number, rangeMilliseconds: number): string {\n32\t    const timestamp = new Date(timestampMilliseconds);\n33\t\n34\t    if (rangeMilliseconds <= WHOLE_DAY_MILLISECONDS) {\n35\t        return CZECH_CLOCK_TIME_FORMAT.format(timestamp);\n36\t    }\n37\t\n38\t    return rangeMilliseconds <= 14 * WHOLE_DAY_MILLISECONDS\n39\t        ? CZECH_DAY_TIME_FORMAT.format(timestamp)\n40\t        : CZECH_DAY_FORMAT.format(timestamp);\n41\t}\n42\t\n43\t/**\n44\t * Names the moment one point of the overview graph begins at, in full, for a reader who asked about that point\n45\t */\n46\texport function formatWorkshopOverviewPointTime(timestampMilliseconds: number): string {\n47\t    return CZECH_DATE_TIME_FORMAT.format(new Date(timestampMilliseconds));\n48\t}\n49\t\n50\t/**\n51\t * Names the audience which really entered the room, in the Czech grammatical number which belongs to its size.\n52\t */\n53\texport function formatWorkshopParticipantCount(participantCount: number): string {\n54\t    return formatCzechCountedNoun(participantCount, ['účastník', 'účastníci', 'účastníků']);\n55\t}\n56\t\n57\t/**\n58\t * Names how many people signed up for a term on the landing page of its event.\n59\t *\n60\t * Note: The noun is deliberately left out, because these are the very same people who are named `účastníci` once they\n61\t *       enter the room, and both numbers are read next to each other.\n62\t */\n63\texport function formatWorkshopRegisteredParticipantCount(registeredParticipantCount: number): string {\n64\t    return formatCzechCountedNoun(registeredParticipantCount, ['registrovaný', 'registrovaní', 'registrovaných']);\n65\t}\n66\t\n67\t/**\n68\t * Turns the seconds somebody had a room open into a compact, human-readable duration.\n69\t *\n70\t * Note: This is the time the room was open rather than the time somebody was really in front of it. Whether an open\n71\t *       room was actively or passively attended is measured by `workshopAttendance` and drawn by the overview graph.\n72\t */\n73\texport function formatWorkshopPresenceDuration(activeDurationSeconds: number): string {\n74\t    if (activeDurationSeconds < 60) {\n75\t        return 'méně než minutu';\n76\t    }\n77\t\n78\t    const totalMinutes = Math.floor(activeDurationSeconds / 60);\n79\t    const hours = Math.floor(totalMinutes / 60);\n80\t    const minutes = totalMinutes % 60;\n81\t    return hours === 0 ? `${minutes} min` : minutes === 0 ? `${hours} h` : `${hours} h ${minutes} min`;\n82\t}\n83\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c05e6a4c-57b2-46a2-a684-8190a40c180e","uuid":"272fe435-ea9f-409c-9fc1-e18a1b4c80c9","timestamp":"2026-09-16T18:03:06.825Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\me\\work\\promptbook-experiments-and-landing-pages\\aldaron\\businesses\\workshop-admin\\workshopAdminFormatting.ts","content":"import { formatCzechCountedNoun } from '@/lib/language/czechNumbers';\n\nconst CZECH_DATE_TIME_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ', { dateStyle: 'short', timeStyle: 'short' });\nconst CZECH_CLOCK_TIME_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ', { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });\nconst CZECH_DAY_TIME_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ', {\n    day: 'numeric',\n    month: 'numeric',\n    hour: '2-digit',\n    minute: '2-digit',\n});\nconst CZECH_DAY_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('cs-CZ', { day: 'numeric', month: 'numeric' });\n\n/**\n * A span of time which is still read as a clock, above which the day has to be named as well\n */\nconst WHOLE_DAY_MILLISECONDS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1_000;\n\n/**\n * Formats a server timestamp consistently across the workshop administration.\n */\nexport function formatWorkshopAdminDateTime(timestamp: string): string {\n    return CZECH_DATE_TIME_FORMAT.format(new Date(timestamp));\n}\n\n/**\n * Names one moment of the overview graph as shortly as the shown span allows\n *\n * Note: An hour-long workshop is read as a clock, a week of a permanent room by the day, so the axis never repeats the\n *       very same date under every single tick.\n */\nexport function formatWorkshopOverviewAxisTime(timestampMilliseconds: number, rangeMilliseconds: number): string {\n    const timestamp = new Date(timestampMilliseconds);\n\n    if (rangeMilliseconds <= WHOLE_DAY_MILLISECONDS) {\n        return CZECH_CLOCK_TIME_FORMAT.format(timestamp);\n    }\n\n    return rangeMilliseconds <= 14 * WHOLE_DAY_MILLISECONDS\n        ? CZECH_DAY_TIME_FORMAT.format(timestamp)\n        : CZECH_DAY_FORMAT.format(timestamp);\n}\n\n/**\n * Names the moment one point of the overview graph begins at, in full, for a reader who asked about that point\n */\nexport function formatWorkshopOverviewPointTime(timestampMilliseconds: number): string {\n    return CZECH_DATE_TIME_FORMAT.format(new Date(timestampMilliseconds));\n}\n\n/**\n * Names the audience which really entered the room, in the Czech grammatical number which belongs to its size.\n */\nexport function formatWorkshopParticipantCount(participantCount: number): string {\n    return formatCzechCountedNoun(participantCount, ['účastník', 'účastníci', 'účastníků']);\n}\n\n/**\n * Names how many people signed up for a term on the landing page of its event.\n *\n * Note: The noun is deliberately left out, because these are the very same people who are named `účastníci` once they\n *       enter the room, and both numbers are read next to each other.\n */\nexport function formatWorkshopRegisteredParticipantCount(registeredParticipantCount: number): string {\n    return formatCzechCountedNoun(registeredParticipantCount, ['registrovaný', 'registrovaní', 'registrovaných']);\n}\n\n/**\n * Turns the seconds somebody had a room open into a compact, human-readable duration.\n *\n * Note: This is the time the room was open rather than the time somebody was really in front of it. Whether an open\n *       room was actively or passively attended is measured by `workshopAttendance` and drawn by the overview graph.\n */\nexport function formatWorkshopPresenceDuration(activeDurationSeconds: number): string {\n    if (activeDurationSeconds < 60) {\n        return 'méně než minutu';\n    }\n\n    const totalMinutes = Math.floor(activeDurationSeconds / 60);\n    const hours = Math.floor(totalMinutes / 60);\n    const minutes = totalMinutes % 60;\n    return hours === 0 ? `${minutes} min` : minutes === 0 ? `${hours} h` : `${hours} h ${minutes} min`;\n}\n","numLines":83,"startLine":1,"totalLines":83}}}

= Math.max(0, Math.floor(durationInSeconds));\n    const seconds = wholeSeconds % SECONDS_PER_MINUTE;\n    const wholeMinutes = Math.floor(wholeSeconds / SECONDS_PER_MINUTE);\n    const minutes = {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01M8uFXqNeF9ysfV8LLkGsiy","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Current preversion\n2\t\n3\t- Let the project a term is about run in more than one place. The project settings of `/admin/workshops` now take one\n4\t  address of a deployment per line instead of a single address altogether, and\n5\t  `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` opens every one of them beside the repository the workshop follows. A\n6\t  project deployed in one place is still simply its `Živá aplikace`, exactly as it was; several deployments are named\n7\t  by the addresses they are reached at — `workshop.example/app` beside `staging.workshop.example/app` — because one\n8\t  repeated name would say nothing about which of them a participant is opening. The compact card of the term in\n9\t  `/cs/komunita` is previewed from the first written address, so a card still costs one request however many places\n10\t  the project runs at, and the settings export writes them all on one line. Every deployment belongs to the connected\n11\t  repository exactly as its branch patterns already did: they are written, changed and cleared as one connection, so\n12\t  clearing the repository can leave behind no address of a project nobody is connected to. An address which cannot be\n13\t  opened, and a second address which means the very same page, are refused when written and left out when read, while\n14\t  an address stored before this change keeps its place as the first deployment of its project.\n15\t\n16\t- An administrator in `/admin/workshops` or a moderator in\n17\t  `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` can now turn any chat comment into an immediately available material.\n18\t  The source comment remains in the chat untouched; the new material keeps its complete Markdown body and names its\n19\t  chat author in the title. Both entry points use the ordinary material-creation path, so its short links, live room\n20\t  refresh, publication and member access behave exactly like a material created in the content editor.\n21\t\n22\t- Made the compact cards of the published terms in `/cs/komunita` tell more of the story of an event without giving\n23\t  the calendar and the card-list two versions of it: the same card is shown below a selected calendar day, below a\n24\t  month, and in the `Karty` view, and can now show the anonymous average of the star ratings with its count, a visual\n25\t  preview of the project the workshop followed, and the real replay length. That length is the total public YouTube\n26\t  duration less the start offset an administrator set to remove the waiting room, so `1:30:00` with a `75`-second\n27\t  offset is named `1:28:45` rather than pretending the whole live stream is replay. Ratings are reduced before the\n28\t  browser receives them — no response, author, or e-mail is published — and the raw recording identifier stays on the\n29\t  server as well. A missing rating, project, deploy-preview, video, or public duration simply leaves that small part\n30\t  off the card; the ordinary event link, calendar subscription, and membership gate keep exactly their former jobs.\n31\t\n32\t- A term which has only just been held is no longer one more term of the history. Where an event stands in time is now\n33\t  one of four things instead of three — it is still ahead, it runs right now, it is freshly past while less than a day\n34\t  has gone by since the end recorded for it, or it is past — and that is answered in the single place which already\n35\t  answered the other three, so no list, badge, or colour can decide it on its own. In `/cs/komunita` such a term wears\n36\t  its own amber `Právě proběhlo` badge, colours its own day of the calendar, is named in the legend beside the three\n37\t  others, and is listed after what is ahead rather than at the head of the archive. In\n38\t  `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` it is offered in the open under `Právě proběhlo`, between the workshops\n39\t  which run or are coming and the `Proběhlé workshopy` disclosure, so somebody who was at last night's workshop finds\n40\t  the room they have just left without unfolding the whole history to look for it. `/admin/workshops` lists such a term\n41\t  under `Aktuální a nadcházející`, after what runs and what is coming, because the workshop of last night is the one an\n42\t  administrator is still working on — reading its participants, moderating its comments, publishing its recording — and\n43\t  its `Historie` now holds only the terms nobody is wrapping up any more, so opening a freshly held term no longer\n44\t  unfolds that archive either. Everything which opens only after a workshop is over is untouched: the wrap-up, its PDF,\n45\t  the feedback, and the paid recording all read a freshly past term as exactly as finished as one from last spring.\n46\t\n47\t- A term near enough to be looked forward to is now named rather than merely dated. One held today reads\n48\t  `dnes, úterý 15. 9. 2026 · 11:11`, one held tomorrow `zítra, středa 16. 9. 2026 · 11:11`, and one held later in the\n49\t  same week `tento čtvrtek 17. 9. 2026 · 11:11` — in the gender the name of that weekday has in Czech, so that\n50\t  `tento čtvrtek` stands beside `tato středa` and `toto úterý`. A week runs from Monday to Sunday, as it does in the\n51\t  Czech Republic, and a term further away than that stays the plain date it always was, so a list of distant terms\n52\t  does not grow a weekday it never showed. The waiting room and the term picker of `/cs/online-workshop/participant`,\n53\t  the cards and the calendar day of `/cs/komunita`, the header, hero, term picker and chosen-term line of\n54\t  `/cs/online-workshop`, its thank-you page, and the term picker of `/ai-supervize-mini` all say it, because how near a\n55\t  day is is worked out once, from the day a term falls on in Prague and the day the page was built on. That day comes\n56\t  from the server rather than from the browser, so a page says exactly what it was sent as instead of renaming its\n57\t  terms the instant it hydrates. Nothing which is not a term read against today changed: the times of chat messages and\n58\t  materials, the dates a membership is paid to, the printed participant sheet, the published calendar, and the notes a\n59\t  registration is counted by are untouched.\n60\t\n61\t- Moved the community polls attached to an occurrence to the bottom of `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=`.\n62\t  A participant now reads the stage, the invitation, and everything the workshop hands over in its materials first, and\n63\t  is asked for their vote below them, because a poll a workshop is merely the subject of matters less to its\n64\t  participant than the materials they came for. The poll itself, its options, its written answers and the one shared\n65\t  e-mail-owned vote are unchanged, and `/cs/komunita` keeps its own polls above its materials, because that is where\n66\t  the community makes its decisions rather than being asked about somebody else's. Where the polls of a room belong is\n67\t  now decided once, by the kind of that room, so the two rooms cannot drift into their own orders.\n68\t\n69\t- Let `/cs/komunita` list the conferences and workshops which lecturers of the community speak at elsewhere. A term of\n70\t  the new `Externí akce` kind of event is administered in `/admin/workshops` beside every other term and carries one\n71\t  thing the terms held here never do: the address of its organizer, which is where its card and its calendar day lead,\n72\t  opened beside the room rather than instead of it. It is otherwise an ordinary term, so it is dated, placed, priced,\n73\t  coloured by whether it is over, running or still ahead, and published to `/cs/komunita/calendar.ics` exactly like\n74\t  the rest. Because such an event is held by somebody else, this application runs no room and gathers no registration\n75\t  for it: its administration says so rather than reporting an audience of nobody, the membership never returns a payer\n76\t  to somebody else's website, and a term whose address is missing is refused when written and offered nowhere if it\n77\t  was ever stored without one.\n78\t\n79\t- An administrator can now enable an `Other` answer for a community poll. In both `/cs/komunita` and an attached\n80\t  `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` room, a member can write an answer which immediately becomes a normal,\n81\t  anonymous option and receives that member's shared e-mail-owned vote at the same time. Everyone can then vote for\n82\t  it from either room; duplicate wording reuses the existing option, and later administration edits keep member-written\n83\t  answers intact.\n84\t\n85\t- After an online workshop has its recorded end, `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` now offers its attendee a\n86\t  downloadable, paginated wrap-up PDF. It uses the same participant-visible workshop description, takeaways already\n87\t  authored in material titles, headings and lists, and material text/links the room already unlocked for that person;\n88\t  the public presentation is included too. The PDF is created locally only when requested, so it adds no admin setting,\n89\t  database record, or new source of material access.\n90\t\n91\t- Added a configurable start offset in seconds to the stage settings of `/admin/workshops`. After an online workshop\n92\t  ends, `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` now opens the paid member replay at that position, so the same\n93\t  uploaded stream can skip its empty waiting room without a second trimmed upload. The countdown and live stream are\n94\t  unchanged; members without replay access still receive only the existing teaser or membership offer.\n95\t\n96\t- Placed the community material of `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` by what the member reading it has: a\n97\t  participant who does not pay for the membership is invited into the community before the materials of the workshop,\n98\t  while a paying member keeps that invitation at the end of the list as one more way on. The card itself, its link and\n99\t  the identity it carries are unchanged, and the presentation and the project of a workshop stay where they were. Every\n100\t  card which shares the material list now says where among the ordinary materials it belongs, so one rule places them\n101\t  all instead of each room deciding its own order.\n102\t\n103\t- Added a presentation setting to `/admin/workshops`. A workshop can now link a PDF, PowerPoint file, or public GitHub\n104\t  Markdown page, and `/cs/online-workshop/participant?workshop=` shows it beside ordinary materials with the same\n105\t  open action and desktop QR code. The presentation is a shared workshop-level material, so it is immediately visible\n106\t  to free and paid participants alike without becoming timed or membership-gated content.\n107\t\n108\t- Moved a connected GitHub repository in `/cs/online-workshop/participant` into the materials list as a special\n109\t  material. Its existing repository, deployment, and live-commit links now stay with ordinary workshop materials,\n110\t  are visible even when no ordinary material has been unlocked, and remain available to both free and paid\n111\t  participants without turning the repository into timed or membership-gated content.\n112\t\n113\t- Moved the community hand-off in `/cs/online-workshop/participant` into the materials list as a dedicated\n114\t  community material. It is shown even before an administrator has unlocked any ordinary material and remains\n115\t  available to free and paid members alike, while carrying the participant identity through the existing shared\n116\t  community link. The material list now has one reusable special-material slot for room features that belong beside\n117\t  ordinary materials without becoming timed or membership-gated workshop content.\n118\t\n119\t- Let an administrator make a prefix discount code by ending it in `*`: `SUMMER*` now gives its configured discount\n120\t  to every submitted code starting with `SUMMER`. The same database resolver supplies form previews and the atomic\n121\t  registration consumption, so one path cannot accept a code which the other would reject; an exact code takes\n122\t  precedence over a pattern, then the more specific prefix wins.\n123\t\n124\t- Let `/admin/workshops` reopen a workshop by clearing its recorded end, and give an open-ended workshop quick choices to end now, one hour after its start, or two hours after its start; each choice uses the existing live update, so `/cs/online-workshop/participant` immediately keeps or replaces the stream accordingly.\n125\t- Let a paid community member open their Stripe Customer Portal from the membership popup of `/cs/komunita`, through\n126\t  a new short-lived, authenticated link which belongs only to that member and returns them to the community. The\n127\t  portal is now available alongside, rather than instead of, the confirmed in-app cancellation and reactivation of\n128\t  the next renewal, so card and invoice management stays with Stripe while the simple cancellation remains where the\n129\t  member already sees their membership.\n130\t\n131\t- Let a paid member manage renewal directly in the membership popup of `/cs/komunita`: after an explicit confirmation,\n132\t  they can stop the next Stripe payment without losing the days they have already paid for. The modal and its header\n133\t  badge say that the membership is ending and name the last paid day, then offer one-click reactivation until that day.\n134\t  The room saves and reads this intent through the same subscription-state mapping as the Stripe webhook, so a refresh,\n135\t  a later payment event and the member-facing state cannot disagree.\n136\t\n137\t- Moved the community membership surface out of the `/cs/komunita` content column into the room’s shared popup\n138\t  modal. Both the `Free členství` and `Placené členství` header badges now open it, so a member can see their current\n139\t  status or the paid plan, agree to the terms, apply a discount, and enter the same Stripe checkout without leaving\n140\t  the community or scrolling past its materials. A return from Stripe opens that modal as well, preserving the clear\n141\t  paid or cancelled result the in-page surface previously showed.\n142\t\n143\t- Added the paid-membership administration to `/admin/community`: its new `Placená členství` tab pages, filters and\n144\t  sorts the durable payment records by name, e-mail, lifecycle status and Stripe environment, shows the price,\n145\t  discount, payment identifiers and important lifecycle dates, and opens the exact checkout or subscription in Stripe\n146\t  for the payment changes which Stripe remains authoritative for. The existing `Účastníci` table now gives every\n147\t  community session the same shared membership-status badge, including the explicit free state, from one batched\n148\t  e-mail lookup. Each badge opens that member's payment record and each payment record opens their community\n149\t  participant history, so the two administration views stay directly connected without pretending one room session is\n150\t  the durable paid membership.\n151\t\n152\t- Show every visible community poll attached to an occurrence inside that occurrence's participant room, including its\n153\t  current aggregate and the same attached-workshop labels the community and administration use. The workshop room reads\n154\t  the poll without copying it or inventing a second voting system: polls remain owned and edited in the community,\n155\t  while one e-mail-owned vote is shown and counted consistently wherever that attached poll is visible.\n156\t\n157\t- Let a member buy the paid community membership inside `/cs/komunita` itself, through the Stripe payment gate, without\n158\t  ever leaving for the public membership page. The room already knows who is reading it, so it asks for nothing but a\n159\t  discount code and the agreement to its terms, then opens the gate for the monthly price this application decides -\n160\t  including a code's permanent discount or the temporary discount it grants for its configured first monthly renewals.\n161\t  The membership of a member is the same membership however often they reconnect, because it belongs to the address\n162\t  they connect with. A\n163\t  member who comes back from the gate has their payment confirmed against it immediately, while the webhook of the gate\n164\t  keeps following the subscription afterwards, so a cancelled membership, a failed payment and a payment which finished\n165\t  after the browser was closed all reach the room. The badge in the room header now says which membership its member\n166\t  has and leads a free member to that offer instead of to the landing page, a paying member is never sold the same\n167\t  membership again, and a member whose payment failed keeps their membership while the gate is still trying. A server\n168\t  which was given no Stripe key offers nothing at all rather than a button which cannot work, and a server on test keys\n169\t  says so beside the payment and names the test card, so a rehearsal is never mistaken for a real payment. How to\n170\t  configure the gate is written in `AGENT_MESSAGE.md`.\n171\t\n172\t- Put community projects through the same moderation lifecycle as chat messages. A regular member's newly shared\n173\t  project waits for a community moderator or an administrator, while a trusted member or moderator has their project\n174\t  approved immediately by the same shared submission policy. Pending cards stay visible only to their author and the\n175\t  moderators deciding them; until approved they cannot be voted on or opened into a public project discussion. A\n176\t  community moderator can decide from the project gallery, and `/admin/community` now has the complete project queue,\n177\t  including rejected cards, so an administrator can approve, reject, and audit every decision.\n178\t\n179\t- Made the material QR codes in the workshop and community rooms compact and square. Their shared renderer now owns\n180\t  the exact canvas dimensions and removes browser baseline space, while each material uses only the code's built-in\n181\t  scannable white quiet zone rather than a second padded white card. The redundant `Otevřít v telefonu` caption is\n182\t  gone; when one material has several links, the short label below each code remains to distinguish them.\n183\t\n184\t- Made every wide table in the administration usable without travelling to its last row first: a shared table viewport\n185\t  now mirrors horizontal scrolling into a clearly visible bar fixed to the bottom of the screen while that table is in\n186\t  view, yet keeps the native scrollbar as a fallback. The participant, contact, discount-code and short-link tables\n187\t  all use it, and their useful identity column — the participant or contact name, a discount code, or a shortcode —\n188\t  stays pinned while the rest is explored.\n189\t- Said on every term of `/cs/online-workshop` which workshop it is. Each card of the picker now names the workshop\n190\t  held on that date and says what it is about, in the very words `/admin/workshops` wrote about that term, so a\n191\t  visitor chooses a subject rather than guessing behind which of four dates the topic they came for is hiding. What a\n192\t  term is about is read from the term itself and is now part of every list of terms rather than of the live room\n193\t  alone, so the room and the list can never describe one term in two different ways. Both landing pages which let a\n194\t  visitor choose between the terms of their event now offer them with the very same card: `/ai-supervize-mini` keeps\n195\t  choosing its terms by when and where they are held, because its terms are the same workshop in another form, and\n196\t  reads their form and price from the administered event instead of from words written into the page.\n197\t\n198\t- Put the terms listed on `/cs/komunita` into a calendar. The terms of every kind of event are now read as a month of\n199\t  a Czech calendar, which is what the room opens on: its weeks start on Monday, its days are dated in Prague, and each\n200\t  day is coloured by whether what is held on it is over, running, or still ahead. Choosing a day narrows the cards\n201\t  under the month to that day, and a day nothing is held on cannot be chosen at all. The very same terms are still\n202\t  read as cards, which now carry that same colour as a badge saying where the term stands in time, so the calendar and\n203\t  the cards can never say two different things about one term. A month a member is in which has no term at all is not\n204\t  opened on — the calendar opens on the month of the term which matters most instead of on an empty grid.\n205\t\n206\t- Offered the whole calendar of those terms to the calendar application of a member. It is published at\n207\t  `/cs/komunita/calendar.ics` and taken either into Google Calendar or into any application which subscribes to\n208\t  `webcal:`, so a term which is published, moved or withdrawn later reaches everybody who took it without anybody\n209\t  deploying anything. The published calendar names no member: it carries neither an e-mail nor a name, leads to the\n210\t  public page of every term, leaves out the permanent community room which is no term of anything, and identifies each\n211\t  term by its own slug, so a renamed or moved term is corrected in a calendar which already knows it rather than\n212\t  appearing in it twice.\n213\t\n214\t- Put the real community on `/cs/komunita/clenstvi`. The window in its header is no longer an invented conversation:\n215\t  it says how many members the community has, shows the newest approved messages of its chat in the order they were\n216\t  written, marks the moderators among their authors, and counts the messages and reactions the members really sent.\n217\t  Only the flight of the reactions is still made up, because nobody is reacting while a landing page is being read —\n218\t  which reactions fly is read from the ones the rooms celebrated most recently.\n219\t\n220\t- Said the rest of the community on the same page out of the same source. The archive block now names the webinars\n221\t  which are really published, each with the day it is held on, and says how many have already been broadcast instead\n222\t  of listing four topics written by hand. A new section below it counts the members, the broadcast webinars, the\n223\t  messages and the reactions, shows the projects members shared with their preview, author and support, and gives the\n224\t  most chosen answers of the community poll. Nothing of it is claimed when it did not happen: a total of nothing is\n225\t  left out, a poll nobody answered is not shown, and the whole section disappears when the community has nothing to\n226\t  show yet. A member is named by their first name alone, so a page anybody can open never carries more of an identity\n227\t  than the room already showed.\n228\t\n229\t- Replaced the stack of repeated registration forms on `/cs/online-workshop` with one clear term picker and one shared\n230\t  form. Every published online workshop is now a selectable date-and-time card, modelled after the picker on\n231\t  `/ai-supervize-mini`; choosing another card keeps the already entered name, e-mail and phone number, updates the\n232\t  selected workshop summary, and records that exact term in the registration and confirmation link. When no term is\n233\t  published, the page still shows a notice rather than a form that cannot be submitted.\n234\t\n235\t- Let the host put a question on the live stage from `/admin/workshops`. In the `Komentáře` section, any attendee\n236\t  question which has not been rejected can now be sent above the stream of `/cs/online-workshop/participant`, replaced\n237\t  with another question, or hidden again; the artificial-comment form also has one action which creates arbitrary text\n238\t  and sends it to the stage immediately. Every connected attendee receives the change through the same private live\n239\t  channel as reactions, while the selected comment is kept as the room's current stage question so late joiners and\n240\t  reconnecting attendees see the same thing instead of missing a transient announcement. The database retains one\n241\t  comment reference rather than duplicating a message body, refuses a question from another workshop or a rejected\n242\t  comment, and clears a selected question if it is later rejected or deleted.\n243\t\n244\t- Told apart the people who really attend a workshop from the people who only have it running. The room of\n245\t  `/cs/online-workshop/participant` now watches whether somebody is at their computer or phone at all — whether they\n246\t  move a pointer, type, scroll or touch the screen — and says so in the presence heartbeat it already sends, so every\n247\t  measured minute of a room is either actively or passively attended. Somebody who is watching without moving a hand\n248\t  for a while stays active, because the room waits two minutes of complete stillness before it decides that a chair is\n249\t  empty; somebody who left the tab open and walked away becomes passive and turns active again the moment they come\n250\t  back. Nothing new is asked of the browser and nothing is stored twice: the very same presence sample which already\n251\t  counted the audience now also remembers how that minute was attended.\n252\t\n253\t  The overview graph of `/admin/workshops` and `/admin/community` draws it: next to `Diváci`, which is everybody who\n254\t  had the room open, there are now `Aktivní diváci` and `Pasivní diváci`, dashed in the colour of the audience they\n255\t  are a part of so that a reader sees at a glance how much of the room was really watching. The active audience is\n256\t  drawn from the start and the passive one is one click away, both are exported into the CSV and the picture of the\n257\t  graph like every other line, and which of them a graph draws travels in its link as usual. The time an individual\n258\t  participant is listed with is now named `Čas v místnosti` throughout the administration and its exports, because it\n259\t  has always meant how long that person had the room open rather than how attentively they watched it.\n260\t\n261\t- Let a workshop have no end at all. A term whose end is left empty in `/admin/workshops` now runs from its start for\n262\t  as long as it takes: `/cs/online-workshop/participant` keeps its stream on the stage and its room open indefinitely\n263\t  instead of declaring the workshop over an hour after it started, which is what an unwritten end used to mean. The\n264\t  settings of such a running term offer an `Ukončit workshop` button which writes the current moment as its end, so\n265\t  the room replaces the stage with the closing wrap-up and its feedback the moment the workshop really ends, and the\n266\t  administration lists the term as finished. An end is still typed in by hand whenever it is known in advance, and a\n267\t  term whose end is open is still announced with the usual length of a workshop where a duration has to be named\n268\t  before the fact, such as in a calendar invitation.\n269\t\n270\t- Made every event term of every kind of event administered from the one place and stored in the one table. A room\n271\t  which happens at a time is now a term of an event: it says which kind of event it is, whether it is held online or\n272\t  at a place, what one seat costs, and how many people fit into it. The administration of workshops asks these\n273\t  questions in the very same fields whether a term is being created or edited, and offering another kind of event\n274\t  means describing it in the event registry of the application rather than migrating the database or changing any\n275\t  page which lists terms.\n276\t\n277\t- Removed the hard-coded terms of `/ai-supervize-mini` from the application. The page now lists the terms which the\n278\t  administration really published: its header, its hero, its dates, places, prices, capacities, the FAQ answers about\n279\t  the schedule, the capacity and the price, the registration form and the participant information page all read the\n280\t  same administered terms, so a term added, moved, withdrawn or repriced changes the page without a deploy. A term\n281\t  which is held somewhere names that place, a term held online says so, and a price of zero is presented as a free\n282\t  event. While no term is published, the page offers a short notice instead of a form nobody could submit. The seats\n283\t  already reserved keep being counted against the very same terms, because a registration written before this change\n284\t  named its term by the day it is held on and that identifier is still honoured.\n285\t\n286\t- Listed the terms of every kind of event on `/cs/komunita`, each with the kind of event it is, its form and place,\n287\t  and its price. Where a term leads is now decided by the kind of event it is a term of: a term with a live room\n288\t  leads into that room carrying the already verified identity of the member, while a term without one leads to its\n289\t  landing page. Community polls about terms follow the same rule, so a poll about a paid workshop no longer offers a\n290\t  room that workshop does not have.\n291\t\n292\t- Added a clickable `Free členství` badge beside the signed-in member information in `/cs/komunita`. It opens the\n293\t  existing membership page with the benefits of the paid membership, while the shared participant-room header now\n294\t  exposes a reusable slot for room-specific member information instead of duplicating its layout for the community.\n295\t\n296\t- Simplified `/cs/komunita/clenstvi` to two easy-to-understand choices: the community and live AI webinars remain\n297\t  free, while one paid membership costs 199 Kč per month and can be cancelled anytime. The paid offer now focuses on\n298\t  webinar recordings and their archive, practical materials, additional content, priority questions and the existing\n299\t  paid-member Discord/community features; it no longer presents Standard versus Premium, annual billing or a free\n300\t  trial. New registrations are stored as a monthly payment request without a trial under a new plan id, while the\n301\t  legacy Standard/Premium plans, their billing terms and previously agreed prices remain supported for existing\n302\t  registrations. Discount codes, personalized name copy and e-mail prefilling continue to work.\n303\t\n304\t- Added click analytics to `/admin/shortener`: every short link now shows its count of recorded public navigations,\n305\t  and its clickable count opens a private, newest-first history with timestamps, IP addresses, referrers, user agents,\n306\t  languages, platforms, and—for landing pages—the time the visitor opened the destination. The list search, provenance\n307\t  filters, sorting, and selected click history are all held in GET parameters, so an administrator can bookmark or\n308\t  share the exact view without exposing click metadata through the public short-link endpoint.\n309\t\n310\t- Moved every community-project mutation out of PostgreSQL procedures and triggers into backend-owned transactions.\n311\t  Creating a project now generates its UUIDs and initial session hash in Node, makes the project room and author\n312\t  moderator together, and validates the member identity there; opening a discussion reuses or creates exactly one mapped room\n313\t  identity; and voting calculates the Reddit-style transition and both cached totals under a locked project row. The\n314\t  forward migration removes the old project-specific RPCs, identity/count/timestamp triggers, and the extension-backed\n315\t  project-ID default, so `gen_random_bytes(integer)` is no longer evaluated by this flow while foreign keys, uniqueness,\n316\t  RLS, and column constraints remain the database's storage boundary. Deleting a community member now removes their\n317\t  votes and reconciles the affected totals in that same backend transaction; a restrictive foreign key prevents a\n318\t  cascading delete from silently bypassing that reconciliation.\n319\t\n320\t- Let a community poll be about workshop occurrences. The editor of `/admin/community?tab=polls` now offers every\n321\t  workshop beside the question and its choices; one poll can name several occurrences and one occurrence can be the\n322\t  subject of several polls. The shared transaction writes those attachments together with a poll and its settings.\n323\t  `/admin/workshops` now shows an attached community poll in a read-only `Ankety` section with its running result\n324\t  and a link to where it is administered, so no poll is editable from two places. Members of `/cs/komunita` see the\n325\t  published attached workshops beneath the poll as identity-prefilled room links, while drafts remain admin-only. The\n326\t  database enforces the many-to-many relationship, accepts only workshop occurrences as subjects, and removes an\n327\t  attachment when either its poll or workshop is removed.\n328\t\n329\t- Added community project sharing to `/cs/komunita`: the room now places a three-column project gallery directly below\n330\t  the workshop links and above the materials, ordered by upvotes. Its home view shows the five strongest projects and a\n331\t  sixth “Další projekty” card which opens `/cs/komunita/projects` for the whole gallery. Members can vote one way per\n332\t  project with Reddit-style up/down controls, changing or removing their own vote without creating duplicate records.\n333\t  A two-step popup starts with only a URL, safely fetches its public Open Graph title, description and image, then lets\n334\t  the member edit the copy before saving the card. Every project also has `/cs/komunita/projects/<project_id>`, where\n335\t  the preview sits beside the existing moderated workshop chat; the author is connected as that discussion’s moderator\n336\t  automatically, while all project sessions still derive from the member’s existing community identity rather than\n337\t  creating a parallel sign-in system.\n338\t\n339\t- Made community polls fully manageable from `/admin/community?tab=polls`: an administrator can now edit a question,\n340\t  preserve, add, remove or reorder its choices, switch voting and member visibility independently, and permanently\n341\t  delete a poll with all of its votes. The same shared poll editor supports both new and existing polls, so the\n342\t  community keeps using the workshop-room administration rather than growing a parallel dashboard. Each option also\n343\t  has a separately recorded artificial aggregate which can be adjusted without impersonating a member; create a poll\n344\t  hidden, seed those counts, then publish it to start the community with prepared results. Members of `/cs/komunita`\n345\t  see only visible polls and the combined anonymous totals, while database-side locking keeps a concurrent close or\n346\t  hide from accepting a last vote.\n347\t\n348\t- Added `npm run backup-database:verify` and its terminal shortcut. It has `pg_restore` read the catalogue of the newest completed `.dump` archive in `backups/`, excluding interrupted temporary files, without connecting to or changing a database. Backup and verification share PostgreSQL-client invocation and platform-specific missing-client instructions, and the backup shortcut now calls only the canonical backup command instead of producing a duplicate `backup.sql`.\n349\t\n350\t- Let moderators and administration-created artificial messages of `/cs/online-workshop/participant` and `/cs/komunita` carry active links while keeping every normal participant's URLs inert text. Eligible links now follow the same persisted ad hoc `ptbk.io` shortener path as materials, including their UTM source record and shortener redirect click measurement; the safe chat renderer opens only those already-shortened URLs in a new tab, so a raw destination cannot become an untracked active link.\n351\t\n352\t- Made the workshop-feedback star picker preview the score under the pointer: empty stars now fill through the hovered score, so choosing a rating is visible before it is saved; the same preview appears while a keyboard user focuses a star.\n353\t\n354\t- Added `/cs/komunita/clenstvi`, the Czech Premium membership landing page for developers, creators and small-business owners. Basic, Standard and Premium come from one inherited feature catalogue and a responsive comparison table; the page defaults to the concrete yearly prices of 1,800 Kč and 9,000 Kč, always shows their monthly equivalent beside the crossed-out monthly price, lets visitors switch to monthly billing, and gives both paid plans a seven-day trial. `fullname` personalizes the page, `fullname` and `email` pre-fill its registration, and the existing workshop `</>` and emoji animations form the community illustration. Community discount codes now validate and combine with the yearly price, limited codes are consumed by the server, and the accepted plan, trial, discount and guaranteed price are recorded with the Contact registration for e-mail activation because this application has no payment provider. The membership terms now cover the price guarantee and operator changes, suspension or termination while preserving non-waivable consumer rights.\n355\t\n356\t- Added community polls to `/cs/komunita`: a signed-in administrator creates a question and two to eight choices from the new `Ankety` section of `/admin/community`, members choose one answer and may change that answer while voting remains open, and everybody sees only the aggregate result rather than who chose it. Ending a poll leaves its result readable and atomically refuses any last-moment vote. The community uses the existing shared room and administration rather than a parallel page, while the new RLS-secured tables, composite foreign keys, transactional poll creation and database-side vote guard keep every choice inside its community and attributable only to its own member.\n357\t\n358\t- Put a branded QR code beside every linked material on the desktop layouts of `/cs/online-workshop/participant` and `/cs/komunita`. Each code carries the persisted public short URL prepared when `/admin/workshops` saves the material, so scanning it on a phone follows the exact same redirect and click tracking as opening, copying, or forwarding the material link; mobile layouts keep the panel out of the way. The shortener and the shared participant room now both use one client-only Promptbook QR renderer instead of loading separate implementations.\n359\t\n360\t- Routed every HTTP(S) material link of `/cs/online-workshop/participant` and `/cs/komunita` through a persisted ad hoc `ptbk.io` short link, including ordinary Markdown, HTML, reference, autolink and bare-URL forms. The participant room no longer posts browser click events: opening, copying or forwarding the same short address is measured only by the shortener redirect, and `/admin/workshops` now derives material totals and its activity graph from those redirect records. Per-participant material-click figures were removed because a shareable public link cannot honestly identify the workshop participant who opened it. The shortener now records whether a link was manually created or ad hoc and which application created it, and `/admin/shortener` can display, filter and sort by both properties.\n361\t\n362\t- Made `/cs/online-workshop/participant` survive a temporary overloaded or unavailable backend after it has been opened once: every successful room snapshot is now kept in the browser under its own workshop slug, for no longer than the participant session, and a failed refresh leaves the stream, countdown, chat and materials on the last known version instead of replacing the room with an error. A small shared status dot in the upper-right corner now quietly changes from green “Připojeno” to amber while the saved version is shown, keeps the detailed explanation in its tooltip and accessible label, and lets a participant retry immediately; it also serves `/cs/komunita` through the common participant room. The room keeps trying with a jittered exponential backoff rather than sending a whole audience back every half minute, and pauses nonessential presence reports until the service answers again; an authoritative missing-room or missing-session answer removes the private saved copy. The `state-changed` broadcasts already sent for every content and setting change in `/admin/workshops` make the next successful refresh replace that copy, so no second cache or migration is needed there.\n363\t\n364\t- Added a small service worker for the online-workshop funnel: the landing page, confirmation and room prepare the already loaded Next.js assets, and every canonical participant document (`?workshop=…`) is saved network-first under that exact workshop selection. When the application server answers with an overload error or cannot be reached, a visitor who has opened that term before receives their local application shell and its matching room snapshot; prefilled e-mail/name URLs and legacy links without a selected workshop are deliberately never reused as a cached page.\n365\t\n366\t- Added the third, post-workshop stage to `/cs/online-workshop/participant`: when an occurrence ends, the live video is replaced with a thank-you wrap-up, a progressively saved star review (low scores ask what to improve first; high scores ask what helped first), and a direct link to the chosen follow-up material. Chat and reactions remain available throughout. One ordinary Markdown material can now be marked as the follow-up; it is highlighted in the material list before the end and is enforced as a single selection per workshop in the database.\n367\t\n368\t- Added the private `Zpětná vazba` section to `/admin/workshops`, with each rating, partial written response, and its linked Contact context. The same feedback joins the existing contact projection, so `/admin/contacts` and its CSV, vCard, and Book exports show a person's workshop feedback beside their Contact records and attendance history without duplicating source data.\n369\t\n370\t- Verified `npm run test-for-ptbk-coder` locally: ESLint, TypeScript, the production build, and the public Playwright suite complete successfully. The two published-online-workshop scenarios remain intentionally skipped when no published workshop is available, while the other nine public scenarios pass.\n371\t\n372\t- Added Playwright end-to-end coverage for the public site without touching `/admin`: the smoke test opens the public landing and information routes, while real `@example.com` submissions cover the footer newsletter, generic and business lead dialogs, qualification flow, podcast subscription, Pavol contact form, online workshop registration, AI Supervize Mini registration and its future-term interest form. The public workshop-room connection is covered too when a published room is available. `npm run test-e2e` runs headlessly, `npm run test-e2e:headed` opens the browser, both terminal shortcuts are available, and every run archives timestamped `.webm` recordings under the git-ignored `tests/e2e/videos/` directory. `npm run delete-test-data` is the separate, deliberate garbage collector: it removes `@example.com` Contact and workshop-participant records through `DATABASE_URL`, letting database cascades remove their dependent workshop activity without deleting data at the end of a test run.\n373\t\n374\t- Added `npm run backup-database` and its terminal shortcut: `pg_dump` now writes the complete PostgreSQL database, including schema and data, as a timestamped custom-format archive under the git-ignored `backups/` directory, using the same server-only `DATABASE_URL` resolution as migrations and leaving no final file when the dump fails. If the PostgreSQL client is missing, the command explains how to install it on Windows, macOS, or Linux.\n375\t- Added one shared database migration runner: Node.js startup now applies `_initialize.sql` and then the remaining pending `migrations/*.sql` files in filename order, tracks their immutable names and SHA-256 checksums in `public.\"Migration\"`, and refuses a changed or missing applied file. The same operation is available explicitly as `npm run migrate-database` and from the terminal shortcut, while a PostgreSQL advisory lock and one transaction keep concurrent server starts and failed migrations safe.\n376\t- Said the short link itself under \"Your shortened link is ready!\" in `/admin/shortener`, which until now read out the display text of the created link — most often the domain of the destination — so the result looked like the very address which had just been shortened, and only the QR code and the snippets below it carried the new one. The display text still wraps the short link in the HTML and the Markdown snippet, and copying the result into an application which takes nothing but plain text now hands over the short address instead of that label alone.\n377\t- Gave `/admin/shortener` the links it had been creating: every short link there is is now listed with what it leads to, when it was made and whether it greets its visitor with a landing page, is searched for by its shortcode, its destinations or its private note, and is edited or deleted from that very list. Editing keeps the address which has already been handed out and rewrites the destinations, the note and the landing page of a link, so a printed QR code can be pointed somewhere else instead of a second link being made for it; a link of the old Promptbook Studio system is neither retyped nor disowned by being edited here. Until now the page could only ever add one more link and never say which ones existed.\n378\t- Let the administration write the short links it lists at all: the service role had been given nothing but the right to insert one, and a link which was ever visited could not be deleted, because the clicks measured on it refused to let it go — they are now removed together with it.\n379\t- Stopped `/admin/community` drawing the community against a schedule it never had. Its graph opened on a \"time of the workshop\" which reached from the day the row was written to this very minute, so months of emptiness were drawn with everything which really happened squeezed into the last pixel of them; it now opens on everything which was ever measured in the room, is not offered a zoom back to that invented span, and says so in its own words instead of speaking of a workshop.\n380\t- Took the bar which places a member inside the start and the end of a workshop out of the detail of a community member as well, because the community has neither. The moments they were seen are said in words, which need no schedule to be true, and everything they did is still listed as it happened.\n381\t- Took the URL of the community out of `/admin/community` altogether: there is one community and its address was decided once and for all, so the settings neither show the field nor send it, the export of the settings leaves the column out, and the administration API now refuses an address written into any room whose kind keeps a fixed one, exactly as it already refuses a schedule and a stage.\n382\t- Replaced the stack of coloured bars in the \"Přehled\" of `/admin/workshops` and `/admin/community` with a real graph of the workshop in time: the audience is drawn across the hour the way a video draws its viewers, next to the messages, reactions, votes and clicks on the materials, all against one axis so that no two scales can invent a relation which is not in the data. Hovering anywhere reads out every line at that moment, dragging over the graph zooms into that span and the wheel zooms back out, and the graph opens exactly on the time of the workshop, from where it can be opened up to everything which happened before it started and after it ended.\n383\t- Let that graph be taken apart and taken away: every line is switched on and off by its own name, which says its number in the shown span as well; the reaction line counts either every reaction or one chosen emoji; and the whole thing is exported as SVG, PNG, PDF or as a CSV of the very numbers which are drawn, zoom, chosen lines and all.\n384\t- Added lines counted from the words of the chat: an administrator writes a regular expression, for example `pomoc|help`, names it, and the graph draws how many messages matched it minute by minute, without the letter case mattering and without an unfinished expression ever reaching the database.\n385\t- Made the whole view of the administration shareable, so a link now carries the room, the open section and everything about the graph — the zoom, the switched on lines, the chosen reaction and the metrics which were written — and signing in returns to that very view instead of to the dashboard as it was left.\n386\t- Stopped `/admin/workshops` blinking every few seconds: the administration reloads itself constantly, and until now each answer took the whole section off the screen and put a spinner in its place, so a graph could hardly be read at all.
